rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the singular predicate زينة and dual زينتا are grammatically permitted with the coordinated dual subject.
rows.anchor: ويجوز «زينتا» وهو خبر الابتداء في التثنية والإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth beautifies and benefits, while children bring strength and defense; together they adorn worldly life, whose fleeting character should deter attachment.
rows.anchor: لأن في المال جمالا ونفعا، وفي البنين قوة ودفعا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and others who boasted of wealth and nobility: worldly ornaments are passing delusion, while only provisions for the grave and afterlife endure.
rows.anchor: وهو رد على عيينة بن حصن وأمثاله لما افتخروا بالغنى والشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying warns against attaching the heart to wealth, women, or authority because each passes from one possessor to another.
rows.anchor: لا تعقد قلبك مع المال لأنه فيء ذاهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children are a trial, and spouses or children may become enemies, supporting caution about worldly attachment.
rows.anchor: إنمآ أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring righteous deeds include obedience performed by Salman, Suhayb, and poor Muslims; they bring better reward and hope than wealth and children without righteous action.
rows.anchor: أي ما يأتي به سلمان وصهيب وفقراء المسلمين من الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the deeds better does not praise worldly ornament; the comparison is rhetorical, as in the description of Paradise as a better resting place.
rows.anchor: وليس في زينة الدنيا خير، ولكنه خرج مخرج قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say these deeds are truly better than what ignorant people merely suppose to be good.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خير في التحقيق مما يظنه الجهال أنه خير في ظنهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are the five daily prayers; Ibn Jubayr, Abu Maysara, and ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil hold the same view.
rows.anchor: هي الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas defines them as every good deed, spoken or performed, that remains for the afterlife; Ibn Zayd agrees.
rows.anchor: أنها كل عمل صالح من قول أو فعل يبقى للآخرة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the broad definition of every enduring good deed, which al-Qurtubi also calls correct because any deed whose reward remains qualifies.
rows.anchor: ورجحه الطبري. وهو الصحيح إن شاء الله لأن كل ما بقي ثوابه جاز أن يقال له هذا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali distinguishes two harvests: worldly wealth and children, and the afterlife's enduring good deeds; God may grant both to some people.
rows.anchor: الحرث حرثان فحرث الدنيا المال والبنون وحرث الآخرة الباقيات الصالحات

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify the deeds as the transmitted glorifications and praises: subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: هي الكلمات المأثور فضلها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Through Malik, ʿUmāra ibn Ṣayyād reports Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab defining them as the formulas of magnification, praise, testimony, and seeking God's aid.
rows.anchor: إنها قول العبد الله أكبر وسبحان الله والحمد لله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report urges abundant remembrance among the enduring deeds and identifies them as magnification, declaration of divine oneness, glorification, praise, and seeking God's aid; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq graded it sound.
rows.anchor: صححه أبو محمد عبد الحق

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Qatada transmits a report in which the Prophet likens these formulas to leaves falling from a branch, saying they shed a Muslim's sins and are treasures of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ غصنا فخرطه حتى سقط ورقه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mājah gives a similar report from Abū al-Dardāʾ: the four remembrances shed sins like a tree sheds leaves.
rows.anchor: وخرجه ابن ماجه بمعناه من حديث أبي الدرداء قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's report from al-Aʿmash, from Anas, compares a dried tree shedding leaves to the shedding of a servant's sins through praise and remembrance; he calls it gharīb and notes al-Aʿmash did not hear from Anas, though he saw him.
rows.anchor: قال: هذا حديث غريب ولا نعرف للأعمش سماعا من أنس

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet met Abraham on the Night Journey, who sent greetings and described Paradise's good soil, sweet water, and barren ground planted by remembrance; al-Tirmidhi calls it ḥasan gharīb.
rows.anchor: حديث حسن غريب

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits the same Paradise planting report, adding that lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh is its planting.
rows.anchor: وفيه فقلت: وما غراس الجنة؟ قال: " لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله "

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mājah reports that the Prophet told Abū Hurayra that each of the four remembrances he was planting would plant a tree for him in Paradise.
rows.anchor: يا أبا هريرة ما الذي تغرس قلت غراسا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the enduring deeds are intentions and aspirations, since deeds are accepted and raised through them.
rows.anchor: هي النيات والهمات لأن بها تقبل الأعمال وترفع

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr identifies the deeds as righteous daughters, reading the contrast between worldly sons and what remains as a promise of reward and hope for fathers who treat daughters well.
rows.anchor: هن البنات يدل عليه أوائل الآية

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha's report about a poor woman and her daughters is cited as evidence for the interpretation of enduring deeds as righteous daughters, with its earlier discussion located in al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرناه في سورة النحل في قوله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report describes a man from the Muslim community being led toward Hell, when his daughters plead that he treated them well; God then shows him mercy.
rows.anchor: لقد رأيت رجلا من أمتي أمر به إلى النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the child promised to Moses' parents in 18:81 was a daughter; she married a prophet and bore twelve sons, all prophets.
rows.anchor: أبدلهما منه ابنة فتزوجها نبي فولدت له اثني عشر غلاما كلهم أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preceding wording, أعمالا is accusative as a specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: و«أعمالا» نصب على التمييز

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ḥabiṭat with kasra on the bāʾ.
rows.anchor: و«حبطت» قراءة الجمهور بكسر الباء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads ḥabiṭat with fatḥa on the bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «حبطت» بفتحها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read nuqīmu with the majestic plural nūn.
rows.anchor: قراءة الجمهور «نقيم» بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads yuqīmu in the third person, meaning that God does not establish a weight for them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد بياء الغائب يريد فلا يقيم الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads fa-lā yaqūmu lahum yawma al-qiyāmati wazn, and says even an enormous eater and drinker may weigh no more than a mosquito's wing before God.
rows.anchor: فلا يقوم لهم يوم القيامة وزن

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says ʿUbayd's statement is not personal opinion; a sound report in Bukhari and Muslim from Abū Hurayra confirms that a huge, heavy man may weigh no more than a mosquito's wing.
rows.anchor: لا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة اقرءوا إن شئتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means the unbelievers have no reward or good deeds to place on the scales; their deeds face punishment, and one with no good deed is in Hell.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم لا ثواب لهم، وأعمالهم مقابلة بالعذاب،

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says deeds as great as the mountains of Tihāma may weigh nothing.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بأعمال كجبال تهامة فلا تزن شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the weighing as metaphor: they will have no standing or worth before God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن يريد المجاز والاستعارة كأنه قال: فلا قدر لهم عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports condemn deliberately acquired obesity caused by overeating and luxury; they indicate excess beyond sufficiency for indulgence and weight gain is forbidden.
rows.anchor: بل يدل على تحريم الأكل الزائد على قدر الكفاية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls the corpulent religious scholar the most hated of men to God.
rows.anchor: إن أبغض الرجال إلى الله تعالى الحبر السمين

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reports the Prophet's warning about later people who testify without being asked, betray trust, vow without fulfillment, and become corpulent.
rows.anchor: ويظهر فيهم السمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acquired corpulence stems from gluttony, ease, and unchecked desire, making a person serve the self rather than God and prone to unlawful conduct.
rows.anchor: فهو عبد نفسه لا عبد ربه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The opening question about Moses is an affirmative question, meaning, Hasn't his story come to you?
rows.anchor: هو استفهام إثبات وإيجاب معناه أليس قد أتاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the opening as meaning, His story has indeed come to you.
rows.anchor: معناه وقد أتاك قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Moses' story had not yet reached the Prophet, so God then related it.
rows.anchor: لم يكن أتاه حديثه بعد ثم أخبره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others place the scene after Moses completed his term and left Midian for Egypt; he lost the route on a dark night.
rows.anchor: هذا حين قضى الأجل وسار بأهله وهو مقبل من مدين يريد مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Moses was protective of his wife, traveling with people at night and separately by day so they would not see her; by God's decree he became separated from the group.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى عليه السلام رجلا غيورا، يصحب الناس بالليل ويفارقهم بالنهار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it was a winter Friday night.
rows.anchor: وكانت ليلة الجمعة في الشتاء

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Moses asked Shuʿayb to let him return to his mother, then left with family and flock; a son was born in freezing snow, the route was lost, the flock scattered, and his fire striker failed.
rows.anchor: استأذن موسى شعيبا في الرجوع إلى والدته فأذن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses noticed a distant fire on the left side of the road and told his family to remain where they were; amkuthū means stay.
rows.anchor: أي أقيموا بمكانكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses saw the fire in a jujube tree and marveled that its green beauty remained despite the fire's heat and brightness.
rows.anchor: فإذا النار في شجرة عناب، فوقف متعجبا من حسن ذلك الضوء

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī relates that the fire appeared in a thorn tree, receded as Moses approached, then drew near after he felt fear, and God spoke from the tree.
rows.anchor: فرأى النار فيما روي وهي في شجرة من العليق

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī distinguishes what Moses perceived as fire from what God made it: light.
rows.anchor: الماوردي: كانت عند موسى نارا، وكانت عند الله تعالى نورا

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads li-ahlihi amkuthū with a ḍamma on the hāʾ, also in al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «لأهله امكثوا» بضم الهاء، وكذا في «القصص»

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās explains Hamza's reading as preserving the pronoun's original form, an allowed dialect, though Hamza departs from his usual practice only in these two places.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس وهذا على لغة من قال: مررت بهو يا رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says amkuthū rather than aqīmū because إقامة implies permanence, while remaining may be temporary.
rows.anchor: وقال: «امكثوا» ولم يقل أقيموا، لأن الإقامة تقتضي الدوام، والمكث ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī glosses ānastu as I saw.
rows.anchor: «وآنست» أبصرت، قاله ابن الأعرابي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet told Bashīr ibn al-Khaṣāṣiyya, who was walking among graves in sandals, to remove them; Bashīr complied.
rows.anchor: «إذا كنت في مثل هذا المكان فاخلع نعليك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth interpretation takes removing the sandals as emptying Moses' heart of family and children, since household may be represented by sandals; wearing two sandals in a dream may signify marriage.
rows.anchor: وقول خامس: إن ذلك عبارة عن تفريغ قلبه من أمر الأهل والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God spread a carpet of light and guidance, which Moses should not tread with sandals.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن الله تعالى بسط له بساط النور والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may have been Moses' first religious obligation, as the first command to Muhammad was to warn, exalt God, purify clothes, and shun idols.
rows.anchor: قم فأنذر * وربك فكبر * وثيابك فطهر * والرجز فاهجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses removed his sandals and cast them behind the valley.
rows.anchor: الثانية: في الخبر أن موسى عليه السلام خلع نعليه وألقاهما من وراء الوادي

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ relates that when Ibn Masʿūd visited Abū Mūsā, he questioned him for removing his sandals in his own house, asking if he were in the sacred valley.
rows.anchor: فقال عبد الله: أبالوادي المقدس أنت؟!

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Muslim's report from Anas confirms that the Prophet sometimes prayed wearing sandals.
rows.anchor: أكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي في نعلين؟ قال: نعم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
rows.claim: Al-Nasāʾī reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib that on the day of the conquest the Prophet placed his sandals to his left.
rows.anchor: ورواه النسائي عن عبد الله بن السائب: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى يوم الفتح

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that Gabriel told the Prophet his sandals contained filth; the Prophet instructed worshippers to inspect and wipe dirt or harm from sandals before praying in them; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq graded it sound.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن جبريل أتاني فأخبرني أن فيهما قذرا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about Gabriel reconciles the sandal narrations; scholars agree prayer is allowed in clean sandals, and some consider it preferable by the command to wear adornment at every mosque.
rows.anchor: ولم يختلف العلماء في جواز الصلاة في النعل إذا كانت طاهرة من ذكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about taking one's adornment at every mosque can support the view that prayer in clean sandals is preferable.
rows.anchor: خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī says he wished a needy person would come and take the sandals of those who remove them.
rows.anchor: لوددت أن محتاجا جاء فأخذها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the instruction to remove one's sandals between one's feet during prayer.
rows.anchor: إذا صلى أحدكم فليخلع نعليه بين رجليه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra advises al-Maqburī to place removed sandals between the feet so they do not inconvenience another Muslim.
rows.anchor: ولا تؤذ بهما مسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's placing sandals to his left applies when leading or praying alone; a follower should avoid harming the person on the left, and should place them ahead rather than between the feet.
rows.anchor: فإن كنت إماما أو وحدك فافعل ذلك إن أحببت

rows.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim calls placing sandals between one's feet an innovation.
rows.anchor: وضع الرجل نعليه بين قدميه بدعة

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Agreed major impurities such as blood, human excrement, and urine require washing with water to purify sandals or footwear.
rows.anchor: لم يطهرها إلا الغسل بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maliki jurists differ whether rubbing earth purifies sandals or leather socks from disputed animal urine and wet dung.
rows.anchor: فهل يطهرها المسح بالتراب من النعل والخف أو لا؟ قولان عندنا

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي وأبو ثور
rows.claim: Al-Awzāʿī and Abū Thawr allow earth-rubbing without qualification for such animal impurities.
rows.anchor: وأطلق الإجزاء بمسح ذلك بالتراب من غير تفصيل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says dried filth is removed by scraping and rubbing, while wet filth, including urine, requires washing.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: يزيله إذا يبس الحك والفرك، ولا يزيل رطبه إلا الغسل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that none of those impurities is purified except with water.
rows.anchor: لا يطهر شيئا من ذلك كله إلا الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the view that rubbing purifies filth from leather socks and sandals, based on the report of Abū Saʿīd.
rows.anchor: والصحيح قول من قال: إن المسح يطهره من الخف والنعل لحديث أبي سعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: References to God forgetting people mean abandoning them, never literal forgetfulness; nasiya an āyah means leaving it, and remembrance can mean knowledge rather than recollection.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى لا ينسى وإنما معناه تركهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine remembrance in the report about remembering God means that God knows; likewise remembering a prayer means knowing it is due.
rows.anchor: فكذلك يكون معنى قوله: «إذا ذكرها» أي علمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An overdue human debt is not canceled when its due time arrives unless the creditor releases it; God's obligations are even less likely to lapse without His permission.
rows.anchor: وهي مما يسقطها الإبراء كان في ديون الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy with the agreed requirement to make up an intentionally missed Ramadan day, an intentionally missed prayer must also be made up.
rows.anchor: لو ترك يوما من رمضان متعمدا بغير عذر لوجب قضاؤه فكذلك الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik is reported to say that one who deliberately abandons prayer never makes it up; al-Qurtubi reads this as either saying the past cannot return or as severe warning, like reports on deliberate fasting.
rows.anchor: من ترك الصلاة متعمدا لا يقضي أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even on the severe-warning reading, the person must make up the prayer in place of its performance and repent; God then decides the outcome.
rows.anchor: ومع هذا فلا بد من توفية التكليف حقه بإقامة القضاء مقام الأداء

rows.speaker: أبو المطوس
rows.claim: Abū al-Muṭawwis reports from his father, from Abū Hurayra, a report that a deliberately missed Ramadan fast is not compensated even by lifelong fasting; al-Qurtubi calls the Abu Dawud report weak and, if sound, severe warning.
rows.anchor: وهذا يحتمل أن لو صح كان معناه التغليظ وهو حديث ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound reports establish expiation and include making up the missed day.
rows.anchor: وقد جاءت الكفارة بأحاديث صحاح، وفي بعضها قضاء اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to make up a prayer after sleep or forgetfulness specifies that the sleeper is exempt from sin, not from the obligation, unlike a child before puberty.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالرفع هنا رفع المأثم لا رفع الفرض عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that someone who remembers a missed prayer during an obligatory prayer should finish the current one and then pray the missed one; its transmitter ʿUmar ibn Abī ʿUmar is unknown.
rows.anchor: إذا ذكر أحدكم صلاة وهو في صلاة مكتوبة فليبدأ بالتي هو فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If authentic, the Ibn Abbas report supports al-Shāfiʿī's preference to begin with the current prayer.
rows.anchor: وهذا لو صح كان حجة للشافعي في البداءة بصلاة الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the sound report of Jābir: at the Trench, the Prophet prayed the missed ʿAṣr after sunset and then prayed Maghrib, explicitly beginning with the missed prayer.
rows.anchor: فصلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العصر بعد ما غربت الشمس، ثم صلى بعدها المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Trench report is especially clear because Maghrib has a single narrow time according to the Malikis and al-Shāfiʿī.
rows.anchor: ولا سيما والمغرب وقتها واحد مضيق غير ممتد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from Abū ʿUbayda, from his father, that at the Trench the Prophet made up four prayers in sequence: noon, afternoon, sunset, then night.
rows.anchor: ثم أقام فصلى الظهر، ثم أقام فصلى العصر، ثم أقام فصلى المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars cite these reports for making up multiple missed prayers in the order they were missed when remembered together.
rows.anchor: وبهذا استدل العلماء على أن من فاتته صلاة قضاها مرتبة كما فاتته

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: When one missed prayer is remembered during the tight time of a current prayer, Malik, al-Layth, al-Zuhrī, and others begin with the missed prayer, even if the current prayer's time expires.
rows.anchor: يبدأ بالفائتة وإن خرج وقت الحاضرة

rows.speaker: الحسن والشافعي
rows.claim: A second view, held by al-Ḥasan, al-Shāfiʿī, hadith jurists, al-Muḥāsibī, and Ibn Wahb, begins with the current prayer.
rows.anchor: يبدأ بالحاضرة وبه قال الحسن والشافعي

rows.speaker: أشهب
rows.claim: Ashhab's third view lets the worshipper choose which prayer to perform first.
rows.anchor: الثالث: يتخير فيقدم أيتهما شاء، وبه قال أشهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view reasons from the larger number of missed prayers, since all agree that the current prayer comes first when many have accumulated.
rows.anchor: وجه الأول: كثرة الصلوات ولا خلاف أنه يبدأ بالحاضرة مع الكثرة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik counts five or fewer missed prayers as a small number; some say four or fewer based on Jābir's report, while six is agreed to be many.
rows.anchor: فعن مالك: الخمس فدون، وقد قيل: الأربع فدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether one orders the missed prayer while already praying, all agree that a follower completes prayer with the imam first.
rows.anchor: فكل من قال بوجوب الترتيب ومن لم يقل به يقول، يتمادى مع الإمام

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says the follower should pray with the imam, then the missed prayer, and repeat the prayer performed with the imam; al-Qurtubi says raising it to the Prophet was an error.
rows.anchor: إذا نسي أحدكم صلاة فلم يذكرها إلا وهو مع الإمام

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and Aḥmad say to perform the remembered missed prayer and then repeat the prayer offered with the imam, unless more than five prayers separate them.
rows.anchor: يصلي التي ذكر، ثم يصلي التي صلى مع الإمام

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Al-Khiraqī reports Aḥmad's view: finish the current prayer, make up the missed one, and repeat the current prayer if time allows; if its time would expire, do not repeat it.
rows.anchor: فإن خشي خروج الوقت وهو فيها أعتقد ألا يعيدها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik's apparent view is that someone remembering after two rakʿahs ends after two; if he is imam, his prayer and the congregation's prayer are invalidated.
rows.anchor: سلم من ركعتين، فإن كان إماما انهدمت عليه وعلى من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects that apparent invalidation as inconsistent with Malik's instruction to add a rakʿah after remembering following one, or a fourth after three, then end with a voluntary prayer.
rows.anchor: ولو انهدمت عليه كما ذكر وبطلت لم يؤمر أن يضيف إليها أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو قتادة
rows.claim: Muslim's report from Abū Qatāda says sleep itself is not negligence; negligence is delaying prayer until the next prayer time, and a sleeper should pray on waking and pray the next day at its proper time.
rows.anchor: أما إنه ليس في النوم تفريط إنما التفريط على من لم يصل الصلاة

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: A report from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn adds that whoever catches the next morning prayer should make up the missed one alongside it.
rows.anchor: فمن أدرك منكم صلاة الغداة من غد صالحا فليقض معها مثلها

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī knows no scholar who requires the repeated makeup; he suggests the instruction may be recommended to preserve the virtue of prayer at its time.
rows.anchor: وقال الخطابي: لا أعلم أحدا قال بهذا وجوبا

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: In a sound report, the Prophet's party slept through sunrise, then prayed two rakʿahs and the dawn prayer after traveling; when asked about repeating them the next day, he replied that God accepts repayment from them.
rows.anchor: أينهاكم الله عن الربا ويقبله منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects repeating a missed prayer beyond one makeup, relying on the Prophet's reply and the sound versions of ʿImrān's report, which omit the extra instruction; Abū Qatāda's wording is ambiguous.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ترك العمل لقوله عليه السلام: " أينهاكم الله عن الربا ويقبله منكم "

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet states that one who forgets a prayer should pray it when remembered, with no expiation beyond that; al-Ṭabarī notes some early authorities differed.
rows.anchor: من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not create heaven, earth, and what lies between them in vain; creation points to a powerful Creator whose commands must be obeyed and who rewards good and punishes evil.
rows.anchor: بل للتنبيه على أن لها خالقا قادرا يجب امتثال أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is not purposeless injustice in which wrongdoers and deniers die without recompense, moral command, or prohibition; the opposite of play for the wise is wisdom.
rows.anchor: وهذا اللعب المنفي عن الحكيم ضده الحكمة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses lawh as a wife in the Yemeni dialect.
rows.anchor: واللهو المرأة بلغة اليمن قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan gives two interpretations of lawh: a wife, and a child.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: اللهو الولد وقاله الحسن أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets lawh as a child.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: اللهو الولد

rows.speaker: طاووس وعطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: When asked about lawh, Ṭāwūs, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid answered that it means a wife.
rows.anchor: وجاء طاوس وعطاء ومجاهد يسألونه عن قوله تعالى: { لو أردنآ أن نتخذ لهوا }

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī says lawh may euphemistically mean sexual intercourse, which distracts the heart; he cites Imruʾ al-Qays as poetic evidence for lawh.
rows.anchor: وقد يكنى باللهو عن الجماع

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says any assumed child would be from God's presence, from the people of heaven rather than earth.
rows.anchor: من أهل السماء لا من أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the passage responds to Christians.
rows.anchor: الآية رد على النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also rebuts those who call idols God's daughters: how could something they carved be His child?
rows.anchor: كيف يكون منحوتكم ولدا لنا

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل وابن جريج والحسن
rows.claim: They read in kānnā fāʿilīn as negation, meaning God would not do this, and take the sentence as complete after from Our presence.
rows.anchor: المعنى ما كنا فاعلين مثل إن أنت إلا نذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads the wording conditionally: God is not taking a child, since having one is impossible; otherwise He would not have created Paradise, Hell, death, resurrection, and reckoning.
rows.anchor: لاستحالة أن يكون لنا ولد إذ لو كان ذلك لم نخلق جنة ولا نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says that if God intended a child by adoption, He would choose angels from His presence; some hold this because will may concern adoption but not an impossibility.
rows.anchor: لاتخذناه من عندنا من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes someone reverting to disbelief and worshipping an idol that can neither harm nor benefit him.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي يرجع إلى الكفر يعبد الصنم الذي لا ينفع ولا يضر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses al-ḍalāl al-baʿīd as long error.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الطويل

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī defines al-ayka as dense, intertwined trees, with ayka as its singular.
rows.anchor: الأيك الشجر الملتف الكثير الواحدة أيكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes al-ayka as a grove, while the reading layka is said to name a village; some compare their variation to Bakkah and Makkah.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: { أصحاب الأيكة } فهي الغيضة. ومن قرأ { ليكة } فهو اسم القرية

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ read أصحاب ليكة in al-Shuʿarāʾ and Ṣād; readers unanimously use the genitive form in al-Ḥijr and Qāf, so the disputed places should follow that consensus because the meaning is one.
rows.anchor: وأجمع القراء على الخفض في التي في سورة «الحجر» والتي في سورة «ق»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects Abū ʿUbayd's distinction between Layka as the village and al-Ayka as the land: it is unsupported and contradicts exegetes and Arabic scholars.
rows.anchor: فشيء لا يثبت ولا يعرف من قاله فيثبت علمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Shuʿayb was sent to two communities: his own people of Midian and the people of the grove, whose trees were densely intertwined.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال: أرسل شعيب عليه السلام إلى أمتين: إلى قومه من أهل مدين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the grove's predominant tree was the dūm, a kind of doum palm.
rows.anchor: وكانت عامة شجرهم الدوم وهو شجر المقل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the people gathered under the grove's shade during severe heat, then a cloud covered them and burned them once they had assembled.
rows.anchor: فلما تكاملوا تحتها أحرقوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-ayka means trees; lexicographers agree it is dense woodland, and al-Khalīl specifies trees such as lote and arak.
rows.anchor: ولا نعلم بين أهل اللغة اختلافا أن الأيكة الشجر الملتف

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The word layka derives from al-ayka by reducing the hamza and moving its vowel to the lām; the result remains genitive, like a reduced form of al-aḥmar.
rows.anchor: والقول فيه: إن أصله الأيكة ثم خففت الهمزة فألقيت حركتها على اللام

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says a diptote becomes declinable when joined to the article or in construct form, and al-Qurtubi says no one is known to disagree.
rows.anchor: ما لا ينصرف إذا دخلت عليه الألف واللام أو أضيف انصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse calls Shuʿayb merely their messenger for the people of the grove because he was not their genealogical brother; it calls him their brother for Midian because he belonged to them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم شعيب لأنه لم يكن أخا لأصحاب الأيكة في النسب

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Qatada say Shuʿayb was sent to the people of Midian and to the Bedouin people of the grove.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: أرسل الله شعيبا رسولا إلى قومه أهل مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening admonition asks whether the people fear God; the next words identify Shuʿayb as a trustworthy messenger commanding them to obey.
rows.anchor: { ألا تتقون } تخافون الله { إني لكم رسول أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers share the same answer because they all command piety, obedience, exclusive worship, and refusal to demand payment for delivering the message.
rows.anchor: لأنهم متفقون على الأمر بالتقوى، والطاعة والإخلاص في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete the measure and do not reduce what is measured or weighed; weigh with justice and give people their due.
rows.anchor: الناقصين للكيل والوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to deprive people of their goods and not to spread corruption was explained earlier in the commentaries on Hūd and other passages.
rows.anchor: ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين } تقدم في «هود» وغيرها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says al-jibilla means created nature or constitution; its root means to create.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: الجبلة هي الخليقة

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawī lists variant forms of jibilla and glosses the word and its related forms as a large multitude of people.
rows.anchor: وهو الجمع ذو العدد الكثير من الناس

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās lists forms such as jibilla, jibal, and related plurals, with optional deletion of vowels, doubled lām, or the tāʾ marker.
rows.anchor: ويقال جبلة والجمع فيهما جبال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, as also transmitted from Shayba and al-Aʿraj, reads al-jubulla with ḍamma on the jīm and bāʾ; the rest read with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن باختلاف عنه: { والجبلة الأولين } بضم الجيم والباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line says death is the greatest event to pass over the assembled people; al-jibilla is the word used as poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: والموت أعظم حادث فيما يمر على الجبله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In answer to which term Moses completed, Ibn Abbas says he fulfilled the longer and more complete one; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr relays the answer to a Christian, who affirmed it.
rows.anchor: قضى أكملهما وأوفاهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet asked Gabriel about the term, and Gabriel answered that Moses fulfilled ten years.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل في ذلك جبريل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits Mujāhid's view that Moses completed ten years and another ten beyond them; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it weak.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن مجاهد أنه قضى عشرا وعشرا بعدها قال ابن عطية: وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that Moses traveled with his family supports a husband's ability to take his wife where he wishes by his guardianship, unless he has made a binding agreement; marriage covenants especially deserve fulfillment.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يلتزم لها أمرا فالمؤمنون عند شروطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read jadhwa with kasra on the jīm; Ḥamza and Yaḥyā use ḍamma, and ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, and Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والجذوة بكسر الجيم قراءة العامة، وضمها حمزة ويحيى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses the jadhwa as a piece of ember and says this is common Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد في قوله تعالى: { أو جذوة من النار } أي قطعة من الجمر

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī says the differently vocalized forms all mean a burning ember, with several plural forms.
rows.anchor: الجذوة والجذوة والجذوة الجمرة الملتهبة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says jadhwa is like jadhma: a thick piece of wood, whether or not fire remains at its end.
rows.anchor: والجذوة مثل الجذمة وهي القطعة الغليظة من الخشب

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse uses al-jidhā for large pieces of fuel that do not quickly go out.
rows.anchor: جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: This verse was revealed to urge believers in Mecca to migrate: God's earth is wide, so they should leave persecution for a place where they can manifest monotheism.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية نزلت في تحريض المؤمنين الذين كانوا بمكة على الهجرة

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr and ʿAṭāʾ say the verse applies to any land ruled by oppression and wrong, from which migration to a just land is required; Malik agrees.
rows.anchor: إن الأرض التي فيها الظلم والمنكر تترتب فيها هذه الآية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reads the command as an instruction to migrate and struggle.
rows.anchor: فهاجروا وجاهدوا

rows.speaker: مطرف بن الشخير
rows.claim: Muṭarrif ibn al-Shikhkhīr offers two readings: God's mercy is broad, and God's provision is broad and should be sought throughout the earth.
rows.anchor: إن رحمتي واسعة

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri advises moving from an expensive land to another where a dirham buys a basket of bread.
rows.anchor: إذا كنت بأرض غالية فانتقل إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God's broad earth as Paradise, which worshippers inherit through worship.
rows.anchor: إن أرضي التي هي أرض الجنة واسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to worship God uses an understood verb with the object إياي; the fronted phrase adds a conditional sense: if one place is constricted, worship God elsewhere.
rows.anchor: { إياي } منصوب بفعل مضمر، أي فاعبدوا إياي فاعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that every soul dies, also discussed in Āl ʿImrān, diminishes worldly fears: believers concerned about death or hunger in leaving Mecca should hasten to obedience and migration.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكره هاهنا تحقيرا لأمر الدنيا ومخاوفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises believing doers of good Paradise as encouragement, then describes them as those who patiently endure and rely on their Lord.
rows.anchor: ثم وعد المؤمنين العاملين بسكنى الجنة تحريضا منه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb, al-Jaḥdarī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Muḥayṣin, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read yāʾ in yā ʿibādi as still; others open it.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمر ويعقوب والجحدري وابن أبي إسحاق وابن محيصن والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir opens the final vowel of arḍī; the other readers make it still.
rows.anchor: { إن أرضي } فتحها ابن عامر. وسكنها الباقون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that one who flees from land to land for the sake of religion, even by a handspan, merits Paradise and the companionship of Muhammad and Abraham.
rows.anchor: من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض ولو قيد شبر استوجب الجنة

rows.speaker: السلمي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read yarjiʿūn with yāʾ, matching the preceding mention of every soul tasting death; the other readers use tāʾ, matching the address to believing servants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي وأبو بكر عن عاصم: { يرجعون } بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited elegy laments death, warns against attachment to worldly beauty, and asks what became of former loved ones and neighbors.
rows.anchor: الموت في كل حين ينشد الكفنا ونحن في غفلة عما يراد بنا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use lanuthwiyannahum, with thāʾ from dwelling, meaning that God will grant rooms in which they reside.
rows.anchor: { لنثوينهم } بالثاء مكان الباء من الثوى

rows.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب والجحدري والسلمي
rows.claim: These readers use liyubawwiʾannahum with yāʾ instead of nūn; the other readers use lanubawwiʾannahum, meaning God will settle them in rooms.
rows.anchor: «ليبوئنهم» بالياء مكان النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuraf are lofty upper chambers.
rows.anchor: أي «لننزلهم» { غرفا } جمع غرفة وهي العلية المشرفة

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Muslim reports from Sahl ibn Saʿd that inhabitants of Paradise's chambers are seen from below like a bright star on the horizon because of their different ranks; they are believers who affirm the messengers, not Prophets alone.
rows.anchor: لتفاضل ما بينهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from ʿAlī that the rooms are transparent inside and out and belong to those who speak well, feed others, fast regularly, and pray at night while people sleep.
rows.anchor: هي لمن أطاب الكلام وأطعم الطعام وأدام الصيام وصلى لله بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran gives every needed kind of parable to guide people, alert them to God's oneness, and establish the messengers' truthfulness.
rows.anchor: أي من كل مثل يدلهم على ما يحتاجون إليه، وينبههم على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when given a miracle such as the cleaving sea or Moses' staff, disbelievers call believers followers of falsehood and sorcery.
rows.anchor: كفلق البحر والعصا وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of people who do not know the proofs of divine oneness just as He seals the disbelievers' hearts.
rows.anchor: { يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون } أدلة التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their abuse because God's promise to grant victory is true.
rows.anchor: أي اصبر على أذاهم فإن الله ينصرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakhiffannaka means do not let those without certainty provoke you away from your religion; they try to make someone foolish enough to follow error.
rows.anchor: أي لا يستفزنك عن دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify those without certainty as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith; although addressed to the Prophet, the warning is intended for his community.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو النضر بن الحارث. والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is jussive and emphasized by the heavy nūn, so its form is built on fatḥ; alladhīna is nominative, with اللذون another Arab nominative form.
rows.anchor: أكد بالنون الثقيلة فبني على الفتح

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhaylī says Luqmān's son was called Thārān according to al-Ṭabarī and al-Qutbī.
rows.anchor: اسم ابنه ثاران في قول الطبري والقتبي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī names Luqmān's son as Mishkam.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: مشكم

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh transmits another name for the son: Anʿam.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنعم حكاه النقاش

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says Luqmān's son and wife were unbelievers, and he continued admonishing them until they accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: أن ابنه وامرأته كانا كافرين فما زال يعظهما حتى أسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition against associating partners with God supports the claim that Luqmān was instructing his son.
rows.anchor: قلت: ودل على هذا قوله: { لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم }

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When 6:82 was revealed, the Companions feared that any wrongdoing invalidated their faith; the Prophet clarified that the verse's ظلم means shirk, as Luqmān told his son.
rows.anchor: ليس هو كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ whether the statement that shirk is grave injustice is Luqmān's words or a divine comment joined to them; the reported revelation supports the latter, though either attribution could reassure the Companions.
rows.anchor: واختلف في قوله: { إن الشرك لظلم عظيم } فقيل: إنه من كلام لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle idh is accusative as an instruction to remember; al-Zajjāj instead attaches it to āṯaynā, but al-Naḥḥās considers that mistaken because the intervening wāw prevents it.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وأحسبه غلطا لأن في الكلام واوا تمنع من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address yā bunayya is read with kasra on the yāʾ to indicate an omitted yāʾ; some use fatḥa as lighter. Its diminutive form expresses tenderness, not literal smallness.
rows.anchor: وقوله: «يا بني» ليس هو على حقيقة التصغير وإن كان على لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses interrupt Luqmān's advice. One view makes them part of his advice to obey parents outside of shirk; another makes God address Luqmān with a command to thank Him; a third treats them as God's separate instruction to humanity.
rows.anchor: هاتان الآيتان اعتراض بين أثناء وصية لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the correct view, held by a group of exegetes, is that these verses were revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, as previously discussed in al-ʿAnkabūt.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في شأن سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children must not obey parents in committing a major sin or abandoning an individual duty; obedience is required in permissible matters, and yielding on recommended acts is good.
rows.anchor: طاعة الأبوين لا تراعى في ركوب كبيرة ولا في ترك فريضة على الأعيان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan differs on one example: if a mother prevents her child from attending the night prayer out of concern, he says the child should not obey.
rows.anchor: إن منعته أمه من شهود العشاء شفقة فلا يطعها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asked whom he should honor most; the Prophet named the mother three times, then the father, matching the verse's three maternal burdens and one paternal share.
rows.anchor: «أمك» قال: ثم من؟ قال: «أمك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother receives three measures of filial honor because pregnancy and nursing are singled out in addition to parenthood, while the father receives one.
rows.anchor: حصل لها بذلك ثلاث مراتب، وللأب واحدة وأشبه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahnan ʿalā wahn means the mother carried the child with weakness increasing day after day.
rows.anchor: حملته في بطنها وهي تزداد كل يوم ضعفا على ضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that women are weak by nature and pregnancy further weakens them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المرأة ضعيفة الخلقة ثم يضعفها الحمل

rows.speaker: عيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī reads both instances of wahn with fatḥa on the hāʾ; the same reading is reported from Abū ʿAmr, and the meaning is unchanged.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي: «وهنا على وهن» بفتح الهاء فيهما ورويت عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: قعنب بن أم صاحب
rows.claim: Qanab ibn Umm Ṣāḥib's verse uses al-ayn and al-wahn as evidence for the word's usage.
rows.anchor: إن العواذل فيها الأين والوهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word wahn has multiple Arabic conjugations; wahnan is accusative as a verbal noun according to al-Qushayrī, or as a second object with the preposition omitted according to al-Naḥḥās.
rows.anchor: وانتصب «وهنا» على المصدر ذكره القشيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read fiṣāluhu; al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb read faṣluhu. Both are dialect forms for weaning, named by its endpoint at two years.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «وفصاله» وقرأ الحسن ويعقوب: «وفصله» وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists agree that nursing lasts two years for maintenance rulings; opinions differ on milk kinship, including one year only, two years plus an adjacent month if nursing continues, and whether milk after early weaning still prohibits.
rows.anchor: الناس مجمعون على العامين في مدة الرضاع في باب الأحكام والنفقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses an aškur as accusative, meaning God commanded gratitude; al-Naḥḥās prefers an explanatory particle, meaning We told the person to thank God and parents.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وأجود منه أن تكون «أن» مفسرة، والمعنى: قلنا له أن اشكر لي ولوالديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say thanks to God are for faith and thanks to parents for upbringing.
rows.anchor: قيل: الشكر لله على نعمة الإيمان، وللوالدين على نعمة التربية

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna says the five daily prayers express gratitude to God, while praying for one's parents after them expresses gratitude to the parents.
rows.anchor: من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to resist parents' pressure to associate partners with God was revealed about Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ when his mother Ḥamna bint Abī Sufyān swore not to eat after he converted.
rows.anchor: نزلتا في شأن سعد بن أبي وقاص لما أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kind companionship means treating parents with goodness; the verse supports giving poor non-Muslim parents money, speaking gently, and inviting them to Islam with kindness.
rows.anchor: والآية دليل على صلة الأبوين الكافرين بما أمكن من المال

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asmāʾ asked the Prophet whether to maintain her visiting mother or maternal aunt, who had come seeking connection; he told her yes.
rows.anchor: إن أمي قدمت علي وهي راغبة أفأصلها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes rāghibah to mean that Asmāʾ's mother desired her connection, since need likely brought her to visit.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عندي أنها راغبة في الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asmāʾ's mother was Qutayla bint ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAbd Asad; ʿĀʾisha and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's mother was the early Muslim Umm Rūmān.
rows.anchor: ووالدة أسماء هي قتيلة بنت عبد العزى بن عبد أسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to follow the path of those who turn to God addresses everyone; anāba means turning or returning, the way of prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: وصية لجميع العالم كأن المأمور الإنسان

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says the command addresses Saʿd and the one who turned to God was Abū Bakr; after Abū Bakr converted, Saʿd and five others visited and accepted Islam after hearing 39:9.
rows.anchor: والذي أناب أبو بكر

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says Saʿd was addressed and Abū Bakr the one who turned to God; after Abū Bakr converted, six companions embraced Islam, and the cited passage was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أن المأمور سعد، والذي أناب أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the one who turned to God as the Prophet; Ibn Abbas says Saʿd's brothers ʿĀmir and ʿUwaymir also converted, leaving only ʿUtba among them as an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذي أناب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns that all people will be raised and returned for recompense and examination of both small and great deeds.
rows.anchor: ثم توعد عز وجل ببعث من في القبور والرجوع إليه للجزاء والتوقيف على صغير الأعمال وكبيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān tells his son to establish prayer, promote right, and prevent wrong; one must practice these virtues oneself before directing others.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما يريد به بعد أن يمتثل ذلك هو في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem says a person should first restrain his own wrongdoing; only after that can he be considered wise.
rows.anchor: وابدأ بنفسك فانهها عن غيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience under affliction encourages changing wrong even when it brings harm; al-Qurtubi treats this courage as recommended rather than obligatory.
rows.anchor: وهذا القدر على جهة الندب والقوة في ذات الله وأما على اللزوم فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the patience as endurance of illness and other worldly hardships without despair that leads to disobedience; al-Qurtubi calls this a good, inclusive interpretation.
rows.anchor: وألا يخرج من الجزع إلى معصية الله عز وجل وهذا قول حسن لأنه يعم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls patience through hardships a core reality of faith.
rows.anchor: من حقيقة الإيمان الصبر على المكاره

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says prayer, enjoining right, and forbidding wrong are among the matters God has firmly commanded.
rows.anchor: مما عزمه الله وأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says Ibn Jurayj's interpretation is the sounder one; another possibility is that these are virtues of resolute, morally excellent people.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن جريج أصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After setting out legal rulings in the surah, God commands compliance; the amanah, by the sound majority view, encompasses all duties of religion.
rows.anchor: والأمانة تعم جميع وظائف الدين على الصحيح من الأقوال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmits Ibn Abbas's report that God offered Adam the trust: carrying it earns reward and neglecting it brings punishment; Adam accepted, and after a short stay in Paradise was expelled by Satan.
rows.anchor: إن حملتها أجرت وإن ضيعتها عذبت فاحتملها بما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust consists of the obligatory duties God entrusted to people.
rows.anchor: فالأمانة هي الفرائض التي ائتمن الله عليها العباد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the trust includes financial deposits; another report from him says all obligations, especially property entrusted to others.
rows.anchor: هي في أمانات الأموال كالودائع وغيرها

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb identifies a woman's chastity as one of the trusts.
rows.anchor: من الأمانة أن ائتمنت المرأة على فرجها

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says the major ablution after sexual impurity is a trust, the only aspect of religion in which God entrusted the human being.
rows.anchor: غسل الجنابة أمانة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls prayer a trust, since a person may honestly say either that he prayed or that he did not; the same applies to fasting and major ablution.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث مرفوع: " الأمانة الصلاة " إن شئت قلت قد صليت

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says the sexual organ was God's first trust placed in a person, then lists the ear, eye, tongue, belly, hand, and foot as trusts; without trustworthiness there is no faith.
rows.anchor: فالفرج أمانة، والأذن أمانة، والعين أمانة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains the trust through Adam leaving Cain responsible for his family while he visited the House at Mecca; the heavens, earth, and mountains declined, but Cain agreed and then killed his brother.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي هي ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل على ولده وأهله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Maʿmar transmits al-Ḥasan's report: when told good performance earned reward and failure incurred punishment, the heavens, earth, and mountains refused the trust.
rows.anchor: إن أحسنت جوزيت وإن أسأت عوقبت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the trust was offered to Adam after his creation; he accepted responsibility for reward or punishment, and left Paradise within the span from noon to afternoon.
rows.anchor: فما كان بين أن تحملها إلى أن أخرج من الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the trust as religious duties: the heavens, earth, and mountains declined from reverence and concern that they could not fulfill them, not from disobedience, while Adam accepted.
rows.anchor: وروى علي ابن طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says Ibn Abbas's interpretation is the one followed by exegetes.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو الذي عليه أهل التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says that when Adam neared death, he offered the trust to creation and only his sons accepted it.
rows.anchor: لما حضرت آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم الوفاة أمر أن يعرض الأمانة على الخلق

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians define the trust as the evidence of God's lordship deposited in the heavens, earth, and mountains: they display it, while the human conceals and denies it.
rows.anchor: من الدلائل على ربوبيته أن يظهروها فأظهروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ʿaraḍnā means we made apparent, as when a woman is presented for sale; the trust and its neglect were presented to the inhabitants of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «عرضنا» أظهرنا، كما تقول: عرضت الجارية على البيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens' refusal to bear the trust means refusing to carry its burden or guilt, as in the verse about bearing their burdens.
rows.anchor: { فأبين أن يحملنها } أي أن يحملن وزرها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the human who took the trust was the unbeliever and hypocrite, unjust to himself and ignorant of his Lord; this is figurative, like asking a town.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: المراد الكافر والمنافق. { إنه كان ظلوما } لنفسه { جهولا } بربه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the trust and its consequences of reward and punishment were shown to the heavens; they declined out of awe, saying they could not bear it, yet remained obedient to God's other commands.
rows.anchor: لا أبتغي ثوابا ولا عقابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the literal account, inanimate beings would need to be given life in order to understand and answer; the offer was voluntary choice for them but binding obligation for humanity.
rows.anchor: وهذا العرض عرض تخيير لا إلزام. والعرض على الإنسان إلزام

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl and others read the scene as a parable: even the enormous heavens, earth, and mountains could not bear the weight of religious obligations with reward and punishment, yet the unjust, ignorant human undertook them.
rows.anchor: العرض في هذه الآية ضرب مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable resembles the mountain passage in al-Ḥashr, followed by the statement that God presents such parables to people.
rows.anchor: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another figurative reading compares the burden of the trust with the capacity of the heavens and earth; they would refuse if able to speak, just as one says a camel refused a load after comparing its strength with the burden.
rows.anchor: عرضت الحمل على البعير فأباه
